highlights.title: Thousands will die if EPA repeals power plant climate rules, lawsuit says
highlights.summary: Days after finalizing a rule that would eliminate climate rules for power plants, the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) was sued by groups who say the EPA’s repeal was shockingly short-sighted and risked leaving the country’s single largest source of industrial climate pollution unchecked.
body: On Thursday, the American Lung Association, the American Public Health Association (APHA), the Clean Air Council, Clean Wisconsin, the Environmental Defense Fund, and the Natural Resources Defense Council (NRDC) filed a petition requesting that the US Court of Appeals for the DC Circuit review if the EPA’s action conflicts with the Clean Air Act.
“Clean air is a basic human right,” APHA CEO Georges C. Benjamin said.

A physician and long-time public health policy leader, Benjamin warned that the EPA was “weakening” “life-saving standards” and stripping away “vital protections for all, and especially for children, pregnant people and communities already overburdened by pollution.” The lawsuit alleges that the rule change could cause thousands of premature deaths.
In the EPA’s announcement of the proposed repeal, the agency claimed that its action was based on “the best reading of the Clean Air Act.” Benjamin disagrees.

highlights.title: Inside the suddenly explosive world of AI safety
highlights.summary: On a sunny July day in Berkeley, California, the country's top AI safety researchers gathered on an unmarked floor of an unmarked building. They had come together for a "war room" to dissect the high-profile cybersecurity incident that had rocked the AI industry hours earlier.
body: No one in the war room was surprised; this was the very thing the third-party AI-safety researchers had been warning about for years. The incident was the latest, though arguably the most egregious, in a series that was eroding trust in frontier labs. It only reaffirmed the importance of their work.

In one meeting room off the main cafeteria, someone was running a boot camp for getting up to speed on the cyberattack. In another area of the office, a group of researchers were investigating whether that same model, or a similar one, had successfully hacked into any other platforms.
The AI researchers were sure of one thing: This was AI’s first big “warning shot.”

highlights.title: Huawei plans Q1 2027 launch of new AI chip as it takes on Nvidia
highlights.summary: Huawei is accelerating the launch of its next-generation Ascend 960DT AI chip as it pushes to compete with Nvidia and close China’s AI computing gap with the U.S.
body: Huawei is moving up the launch of its next-generation Ascend 960DT AI chip to the first quarter of 2027, as it races to challenge Nvidia, the company said on Thursday at its Huawei Connect conference.
The Chinese tech giant had previously planned to launch the chip in Q3 of 2027, a Huawei spokesperson told TechCrunch.

“The Ascend 960DT is expected to be ready in Q1 2027. Ascend 960 chips are launching ahead of schedule, doubling performance and advancing year by year,” the spokesperson said, adding that David Wang, Huawei’s rotating and acting chairman, announced the updated timeline at Huawei Connect on Thursday.
The announcement comes just a week before U.S. President Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping are set to meet on September 24 in Washington, DC.

Lucy Packer - another try scorer against the Wallaroos - is named at scrum-half with fly-half Zoe Harrison outside her. Helena Rowland is reinstated to the midfield alongside captain Meg Jones.

highlights.title: Monster Hunter Wilds ditches one of its most hated features
highlights.summary: While Capcom has been on a hot streak over the last few years, one of the publisher’s most annoying tendencies is adding strange microtransactions to some of its games, like Monster Hunter and Dragon’s Dogma.
body: Previously, after creating your hunter and Palico’s core appearance at the start of the game, you needed a Character Edit Voucher to make additional changes. Capcom sold a three-pack of Character Edit Vouchers for $6.99, a three-pack of Palico Edit Vouchers for $6.99, and a bundle of both for $9.99. While the company occasionally gave out free vouchers, monetizing this feature at all was ridiculous.

Thankfully, Capcom is finally coming to its senses. When Monster Hunter Wilds: Ascendance launches in 2027, editing your character and Palico's appearances will be free. Until then, Capcom will make these vouchers unavailable for purchase on Dec. 3, 2026, while giving all players 10 Character Edit Vouchers and 10 Palico Edit Vouchers for free. The company will also distribute a Special Thank-You Pendant Set to those who previously purchased any voucher pack, which includes the Heavenly Hog and Beezleboar.

Upcoming is the buzzy “Digger,” directed by Alejandro González Iñárritu and starring Tom Cruise, and the capstone to the “Dune” trilogy, “Dune: Part Three.”

This year, North Road Company developed the North Road Films label, with Adelson at the helm. In addition to overseeing strategy at the company, she also identifies both emerging and established talent. She was instrumental in bringing Kane Parsons and “Backrooms” to A24, helping it become one of the year’s biggest breakouts. “I saw this as a great achievement because of how I identified and supported an emerging filmmaker to great success on a movie that resonated with audiences globally,” she says. highlights.title: Neither foam nor feathers - the perfect pillow for my neck and back is filled with buckwheat hulls
highlights.summary: A small cotton tube stuffed with buckwheat hulls gave me firm, cool support that adapts to how I sleep. I thought I found the perfect pillow. Could these three unseat my favorite? Sign up for the Filter US newsletter, your weekly guide to buying fewer, better things.
body: I used to fight with my pillow all night. I would squash it, fold it, flip it over and shove my hand underneath for extra height. Still, I would wake with a tight neck that only my morning yoga practice could straighten out.

When I sleep, I start on my back, but end up sleeping on my side. Finding a pillow that doesn’t give me back or neck pain is a challenge, especially because I have wide shoulders and prefer a very firm bed. For me, a squishy pillow made little sense.

It took me years to realize that finding the right pillow depends on your sleeping position, body type and bed firmness. My journey led me beyond curved neck pillows, foam that stifled my ear and stacked pillows to make room for my shoulders when side sleeping and ended with a buckwheat hull pillow – the solution to all of my sleeping problems.

For more sleep recommendations, check out our guides to our favorite pillows from Coop, the sleep tech gadgets that actually work, the coziest PJs, or see why the Mzoo sleep mask is the secret to napping – anytime, anywhere.

highlights.title: Your robotaxi might be a narc
highlights.summary: In early September, two teenagers got into a Waymo, but then ended up in the back of a police car. The robotaxi company said it detected "a violation of our terms of service involving a firearm," pulled the car over, and alerted emergency services, according to the Los Angeles Times.
body: Waymo notified the police when it detected a gun during a ride, leading to the arrest of two teenagers. The incident exposes the limits of privacy in an autonomous vehicle.

The arrests exposed a lot of unanswered questions about privacy and autonomous vehicles, including what they are recording, what they do with the footage, and how much privacy riders should expect while riding inside them.

Waymo’s camera-covered cars have already been drawn into the debate over privacy and surveillance. On a number of occasions, law enforcement agencies have obtained search warrants for footage captured by its cars, according to Bloomberg. Last year, the LAPD obtained footage of a hit-and-run that was recorded by a nearby Waymo vehicle. During anti-ICE protests in Los Angeles, five Waymos were vandalized and set on fire amid questions about whether the vehicles could be capturing images of protesters that might be used as evidence to identify or arrest them. Waymo does not publicly disclose how many law enforcement requests it receives or how often it complies.

highlights.title: Take good care of your tailbone. I didn’t – and my derriere has never been the same since | Adrian Chiles
highlights.summary: My coccyx still hurts from an extreme cycling challenge almost two decades ago. Is there anything it’s good for? ‘Welcome to middle age.” This is what my GP said to me 10 years ago when I asked her why I needed this pill or that. Being then just shy of 50, that hit home.
body: I interviewed Prof Alice Roberts this week. A writer, broadcaster, academic, anatomist, archaeologist and sometime medical doctor, she knows her bones, and no mistake. I noted with interest that her PhD thesis was titled “Rotator cuff disease in humans and apes: a palaeopathological and evolutionary perspective on shoulder pathology”. I’ve rarely felt so connected with my ancestors, so human, and indeed so ape-like. In an instant my shoulder pain became easier to bear, as I felt at one with a caveman wincing as he reached up to apply the finishing touches to some wall art.

After the radio show I was full of regret that I didn’t get time to ask her about another bone with which I’ve had my troubles: the coccyx. Mine has not been the same since I did some extreme cycling for Sport Relief with Alan Shearer 18 years ago. To this day, every so often if I sit wrong, I get a very nasty kind of electric shock shooting up from my derriere.

highlights.title: Camp Snap’s 110D gives slim retro film cameras a digital upgrade
highlights.summary: Camp Snap is expanding its small collection of screenless digital point-and-shoot cameras with the new pocket-friendly 110D featuring a thin horizontal design first popularized by Kodak film cameras in the 1970s.
body: The 110D is a modern reimagining of vintage analog cameras that used Kodak’s 110 cartridge-based film from 50 years ago.
If you buy something from a Verge link, Vox Media may earn a commission. See our ethics statement.

The Camp Snap 110D’s design is inspired by the myriad of low-cost cameras from companies like Canon, Minolta, and Pentax that used the 110 film cartridges Kodak first introduced in 1972. The cartridges were easy for even novice photographers to use and could be developed using existing machines already capable of processing 16mm motion picture film. Lomography is one of the last companies to still manufacture 110 film, but the Camp Snap 110D offers a similar experience with the convenience of digital.

Like the Camp Snap 2 that launched last June, the 110D isn’t a megapixel powerhouse. It uses an 8-megapixel Sony 1/3.2-inch CMOS sensor paired with a 4.2mm, f/2.0 lens that’s compatible with 30.5mm screw-on filters if you want to experiment with wide-angle or macro photography. If you’re after a matching retro look for your photos, the 110D includes five built-in software filters with vintage, analog, and black and white effects that are selectable using a sliding switch.

highlights.title: Google, Nvidia, and Anthropic want Emerald AI to find space on the grid for more data centers
highlights.summary: A new coalition that includes Google, Nvidia, Anthropic, and Emerald AI wants to find 100 GW of grid capacity for new data centers.
body: Grid software unicorn Emerald AI has formed a coalition with Google and Nvidia that will use the startup’s technology to secure space on the grid for more data centers.

The AI Energy Management Alliance (AEMA) hopes to make demand response — a paradigm in which data centers temporarily reduce their electricity use — an integral part of data center development. Pausing noncritical tasks and shifting some compute loads, AEMA says, could allow an additional 100 gigawatts of data centers to connect to the grid.
The founding trio is joined by Anthropic, and a range of utilities including AES, Constellation, National Grid, and NRG Energy.

Demand response is an old concept that has been used by utilities for decades. It works because the grid is designed with peak loads in mind. For much of the year, demand is well below the maximum the grid can support.

highlights.title: After being sidelined, Boeing's Starliner to get starring role in NASA's spaceflight plans
highlights.summary: As it contemplates a future without access to SpaceX's Crew Dragon spacecraft, NASA will make some key moves to ensure that Boeing's Starliner spacecraft, which has a decidedly checkered record in spaceflight to date, is safer and can continue flying after its Atlas V rocket retires.
body: Multiple sources confirmed to Ars that as early as next week, NASA will announce that it will order two additional Starliner crewed missions from Boeing, pay some of the costs to fix the spacecraft’s thruster issues, and provide support to certify the spacecraft’s launch on a new rocket.

NASA is taking these steps after SpaceX made clear in discussions with space agency officials in recent months that it intends to retire the Crew Dragon vehicle by 2030, if not before. Crew Dragon is presently the only operational spacecraft NASA has available for routine astronaut missions to low-Earth orbit.

After long signaling it privately, SpaceX has begun to publicly confirm its intentions to wind down the Dragon program, a remarkable move given that the vehicle began flying humans just six years ago. However, the company is seeking to pivot toward its much larger Starship rocket, with the intent of launching its more lucrative Starlink satellites and a new megaconstellation focused on orbital data centers.

highlights.title: Rival AI agents, Instinct and Meta’s Muse, both add the ability to make calls
highlights.summary: People can use these assistants to make restaurant reservations and cancel subscriptions.
body: Text-based AI assistants are a hot market, with Instinct, Wajo, Town, Ollie, and Meta’s Muse agent, which launched last week, vying for users’ attention and tasks. San Francisco-based Instinct is one of the most popular of the lot, attracting huge investor interest at what is reportedly a $10 billion valuation.

Instinct’s popularity may now grow even further, as it’s added a new calling feature that lets your agent place calls and act as a concierge. Meta’s Muse, another serious contender in this battle, has also done the same.

Instinct’s founder Noah Shinn announced on X that the buzzy startup’s new calling feature, Instinct Concierge, can do things like book restaurants that don’t take online reservations, get on your dentist’s cancellation list, or sort out problems with your cable bill. The feature is rolling out in early access to some users, with plans to expand to all users in time, he said.

These calling features arrive as a number of rivals had been touting their ability to make calls as an advantage over Instinct; but with Instinct’s Concierge feature rollout, they’re all now in parity with each other on this front.

highlights.title: King Charles warns of 'existential danger' of AI falling into wrong hands
highlights.summary: The comments were made at a summit in Ayrshire with participants from AI giants including Nvidia, OpenAI and Anthropic.
body: King Charles has warned AI executives of the "existential dangers" posed by the technology falling into the wrong hands.
He made the comments at a summit he had convened at Dumfries House in Ayrshire to discuss how the tech can be used to benefit society.
Those gathered at the meeting also included Kanishka Narayan, the UK's AI Minister, the Pope's advisor, and participants from AI giants such as Nvidia, OpenAI and Anthropic.
It comes amid a series of recent warnings from people inside the industry about the rapidly evolving capabilities of advanced or "frontier" AI models and the regulation needed to keep them in check.

highlights.title: An OpenAI Agent Tried to Jailbreak Itself
highlights.summary: The company also disclosed previously unreported incidents in which its AI models behaved in misaligned ways, including uploading files to the internet without being asked.
body: OpenAI announced a new framework on Wednesday for how it publicly discloses AI misalignment incidents, which the company says it hopes will help inform similar standards across the industry. The company is also releasing new information about several examples of AI model misalignment it identified in the past year, including one in which an AI agent appeared to give itself “jailbreaking-like instructions.”

“As models advance and become more widely deployed, decisions about AI development need evidence that people outside the companies building frontier models can examine,” Kai Chen, OpenAI’s newly appointed head of alignment research, tells WIRED. “We don't believe that the AI industry has solved alignment and monitoring to a sufficient degree to continue responsibly scaling at maximum speed.”

body: Cavan Sullivan is poised to make his US senior debut, with the 16-year-old chosen for Pochettino’s 28-man squad for the September/October window. The Philadelphia Union phenom is one of 13 players who could debut for the national team in the coming weeks, with four friendlies to be played across the country. Should he see the field, Sullivan would become the fourth-youngest player to represent the US, a record still held by Freddy Adu.

Several members of the World Cup squad have been omitted to make way for the youth movement. Christian Pulisic misses out after a slow start to his season with Milan, where he has been a bench option for Ruben Amorim. Weston McKennie is also absent, having missed most of Juventus’s young season with muscle fatigue. Folarin Balogun misses out too, probably due to a lack of minutes after his failed transfer to Everton.

highlights.title: Explosive Elon Musk Documentary Likely to Be Dropped by Universal, Report Claims
highlights.summary: Universal is reportedly reconsidering its release of a revealing Elon Musk documentary, despite it receiving rave reviews at recent film festivals.
body: Weighing in at four hours (with a 10-minute intermission), Musk is the work of prolific filmmaker Alex Gibney, who secured access to various figures close to the Grok owner in his personal life, as well as those who comment on his political influence.
But while an informative documentary on the world's richest man would likely put bums on seats, The Hollywood Reporter claims that Universal is now likely to drop the movie's full release.

Universal paid millions for the rights to release Musk back in 2023, before the now-trillionaire fully aligned himself with President Donald Trump. Today, however, there's reportedly hesitancy over launching the film, with the expected outcome now that the movie rights will be returned to Gibney for him to sell again elsewhere.

In a thread on Twitter/X, which Musk owns, former Wall Street Journal and NBC News journalist Matt Rivera recounted watching the documentary at Venice Film Festival, where it received a five-minute ovation, and listed an array of eye-opening details regarding the film's contents.

highlights.title: India-Canada Screen Industry Corridor Takes Shape as NFDC, SASC Sign Pact at Toronto Market
highlights.summary: India’s National Film Development Corporation and the South Asian Screen Council of Canada put their names to a Letter of Intent at the Toronto Film Festival market, launching a plan to connect Indian and South Asian filmmakers with fresh openings across Canada’s screen business.
body: SASC Canada bills itself as Canada’s biggest South Asian screen ecosystem, an umbrella group whose initiatives take in IFFSA Toronto and the South Asian Screen Office of Canada. Its work touches professional and talent development, project development, market access, international engagement and exhibition.

“NFDC has always been about creating meaningful opportunities for Indian stories and filmmakers to connect with the global industry,” said Prakash Magdum, managing director of NFDC. “This collaboration with SASC Canada creates a focused pathway into the Canadian market, giving filmmakers greater access to festivals, industry partners and audiences while expanding the international reach of their work.”

NFDC serves as India’s national body for growing and promoting the country’s cinema, with a hand in production and co-production deals, developing projects and talent, and building the country’s presence in markets and international engagement circles.

The Letter of Intent aims to open a direct pipeline between the Indian and Canadian screen industries, moving films and filmmakers beyond festival discovery and into deeper market and industry engagement in Canada.
